title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
data_curation: STaR turns a large answer-only dataset into a rationale dataset via self-generation. A tiny prompt set P (~10 hand-written chain-of-thought examples) seeds generation over D. Datasets: a synthetic arithmetic set of 50,000 n-digit addition problems (uniform over digit lengths, scratchpad format from Nye et al.), 10,000 sampled per outer loop; CommonsenseQA (12,247 multiple-choice items, 9,741 train / 1,221 dev / 1,285 test, built from ConceptNet, 10 modified CoT prompts from Wei et al.); and GSM8K (7,473 train / 1,319 test word problems). Filtering is by answer correctness: only rationales whose final answer matches ground truth are kept (indicator reward). Rationalization augments the set by re-generating rationales for failed items with the correct answer hinted. Final CQA model trains on 78.2% (rationale generation) + 8.5% (rationalization) of train data; GSM8K on 25.0% / 28.7%. Each outer loop retrains from the original GPT-J (6B, Pile-pretrained) checkpoint, not continually, to avoid overfitting.
curriculum: Not a pretrain->SFT->preference->RL stack but a single self-improvement loop on a pretrained LLM. Outer loop order: (1) few-shot-prompt the current model to generate (rationale, answer) for all of D; (2) filter by answer correctness; (3) rationalize the failures using the ground-truth answer as a hint; (4) fine-tune the original GPT-J on the union; (5) repeat with the improved model generating the next training set, until performance plateaus. Schedule details: 100-step LR warmup then constant LR=1e-6 (Adam); first outer loop 40 fine-tuning steps, increased 20% per loop; batch 8 packed sequences of length 1024 on one TPU-v3. Arithmetic shows stage-wise curriculum (n-digit only after (n-1)-digit mastered); rationalization collapses this, letting many lengths advance at once. Adding unseen 9-10 digit problems at iteration 20 yields out-of-distribution generalization. Keeping few-shot prompts during fine-tuning raises CQA accuracy (60.9->68.8% without, 69.9->72.5% with rationalization).
method: STaR (Self-Taught Reasoner) bootstraps chain-of-thought rationale generation without a large human-annotated rationale set. Core loop: few-shot prompt a pretrained LLM M to produce rationale r then answer y for each question; keep only rationales where y=y_true (indicator reward 1(ŷ=y)); fine-tune the original M on this filtered set; iterate. Rationalization handles items the model fails: feed the correct answer as a hint and ask for a backward rationale, then train on it as if unhinted, exposing the model to hard problems and growing the dataset. The authors cast STaR as an approximation to an RL policy-gradient objective on a latent-variable view p(y|x)=Σ_r p(r|x)p(y|x,r) with reward 1(ŷ=y): greedy decoding reduces variance (biased exploration) and multiple gradient steps per batch mimic some PG methods; the answer-match filter is the reward signal. Unlike Expert Iteration / GPT-f it uses no separate value function or verifier. Base model is GPT-J (6B); GPT-2 fails because few-shot accuracy must exceed chance to bootstrap.
eval_metrics: Accuracy on three domains. Arithmetic (n-digit addition): per-digit accuracy over outer-loop iterations; 89.5% overall after 16 iterations vs 76.3% for a 10k-example no-rationale baseline trained 5,000 steps; few-shot CoT accuracy <1% on 2-digit, but one rationalization iteration lifts 2-digit to 32%; adding unseen 9-10 digit problems yields OOD solves. CommonsenseQA dev accuracy: STaR with rationalization 72.5% vs GPT-J direct-finetune 60.0%, few-shot CoT GPT-J 36.6%, few-shot direct 20.9%, LaMDA-137B few-shot CoT 55.6%, and 73.0% for a 30x larger GPT-3 direct-finetuned (so STaR roughly matches a 30x larger model); gains are +35.9% over few-shot and +12.5% over direct finetuning. GSM8K test: 10.7% (with) / 10.1% (without) rationalization vs 5.8% direct-finetune, 3.1% few-shot CoT, 3.0% few-shot direct. Human eval (Prolific, 20 raters) ranks STaR rationales above few-shot 30% more often (p=.039) and above human rationales 74% more often (p<.001).
key_results: GPT-J (6B) + STaR with rationalization reaches 72.5% on CommonsenseQA dev, matching a 30x larger GPT-3 direct-finetuned (73.0%) and beating GPT-J direct-finetuning (60.0%) by +12.5%. Arithmetic reaches 89.5% overall after 16 iterations (vs 76.3% baseline) with OOD generalization to 9-10 digit sums. GSM8K test accuracy rises to 10.7% from 5.8% (direct finetune) and 3.1% (few-shot CoT).
evolution_note: STaR builds on chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022), scratchpads (Nye et al. 2021), and Expert Iteration (Anthony et al. 2017), turning few-shot CoT into an iterative self-bootstrapping fine-tuning loop that uses answer-correctness as a reward. In the 2022 context it helped launch the self-improving-reasoning line (later STaR*, Quiet-STaR, V-STaR/RFT, ReST) that distills model-generated reasoning traces as training signal, anticipating verifier-reward RL and self-play trends in post-training.
